title: Ten digits under a telephone label
rationale: Collision group phone-vs-order-number, telephone side. The digits sit under a telephone label and fall in the reserved fictional line range, so the reading as a telephone number is supported. The sibling differs only in the leading label.

provenance.inference: Only the label differs from the collision sibling. That the label selects the telephone reading is project inference; the claim supports only the reserved range. Authored by an AI agent run from the cited claims and case reasoning; no scanner output was consulted; unreviewed.

title: Ten digits under an order label
rationale: Collision group phone-vs-order-number. The digit string is identical to the telephone sibling but is labelled as an order reference. A ten-digit run is a legal shape for both; the label is the only discriminator and no source says a label decides identity.

reasons: The digits fit a North American number and an order reference equally; only the label differs.
No numbering-plan or order-reference source was read that makes a label authoritative.
ambiguity.wouldSettle: A project decision, with cited reasoning, on whether a non-telephone label rules out the telephone identity of a well-formed number.

provenance.inference: The identity is left not-established rather than invalid because a well-formed number can be written under any label. Authored by an AI agent run from the cited claims and case reasoning; no scanner output was consulted; unreviewed.

title: Ten-digit Unix epoch seconds value
rationale: Collision group phone-vs-timestamp. A ten-digit decimal that begins with 1 is what epoch seconds look like for dates in late 2023, and also has the length of a national significant number. The key is a time key.

reasons: Length alone does not separate a timestamp from a ten-digit national number.
Whether a leading digit of 1 is excluded as an area code was not read from a numbering-plan source.
ambiguity.wouldSettle: Read the North American numbering plan area-code form rules and decide whether a time-key label settles the reading.

provenance.inference: Arbitrary round digit pattern; no source. Left not-established because the evidence does not exclude the numbering reading. Authored by an AI agent run from the cited claims and case reasoning; no scanner output was consulted; unreviewed.

title: Dotted three-part number under a build label
rationale: Collision group phone-vs-dotted-numeric. The grouping matches the dotted telephone positive but is written as a build or version number. Only the label differs from the positive.

reasons: Dotted three-part digit groups are used for both telephone numbers and numeric versions or OIDs.
The label is the sole discriminator and no source ranks it.
ambiguity.wouldSettle: A standards text on dotted numeric identifiers and a decision on whether the label overrides shape.

provenance.inference: Value reserved by the fictional 555-01xx range; the label reading is project inference. Authored by an AI agent run from the cited claims and case reasoning; no scanner output was consulted; unreviewed.

title: Dashed nine-digit part number in an unassignable structure
rationale: Collision group ssn-vs-generic-id. A 3-2-4 dashed number labelled as a part number. The area number is 000, which the SSA excerpts say is never assigned, so the SSN identity is excluded by structure rather than by label. A structurally assignable twin cannot be authored without a real-looking value and is recorded as unresolved in the research note.

provenance.inference: Area 000 is excluded by the cited claim; the part-number reading is project inference and is not needed for the identity. Authored by an AI agent run from the cited claims and case reasoning; no scanner output was consulted; unreviewed.

title: Same token under an order label in clinical text
rationale: Collision group mrn-vs-order-id. The token is identical to the labeled medical record number but sits under an order label in a clinical setting, where it is as likely a laboratory or prescription order reference. The label is the discriminator.

reasons: An order label names a different identifier role from a medical record number.
The sources state no value format, so shape cannot separate the roles.
The medical and field-label contexts are research-needed.
ambiguity.wouldSettle: A source defining bounded label vocabularies for medical record numbers and order identifiers.

provenance.inference: The claims define an order identifier and a medical record number as distinct roles; that the label selects the role is project inference. The sibling is unlabelled as to kind, so neither identity is asserted. Authored by an AI agent run from the cited claims and case reasoning; no scanner output was consulted; unreviewed.

title: Same token under a generic patient identifier label
rationale: Collision group mrn-vs-order-id (patient-side). A generic Patient ID label does not say which identifier is meant. FHIR defines Patient.identifier with no format and cardinality 0..*, so one patient may carry several identifiers.

reasons: The label does not name a medical record number; a patient may carry several identifiers.
No format is defined, so shape cannot select among them.
ambiguity.wouldSettle: A type-coded form (for example the identifier type code) or a bounded label vocabulary.

provenance.inference: The cardinality claim is observed; treating a generic label as not selecting the record-number role is project inference. Authored by an AI agent run from the cited claims and case reasoning; no scanner output was consulted; unreviewed.

title: Order label with no prescription or clinical wording
rationale: Collision group mrn-vs-order-id (order-side). An order label without prescription wording or medical context could be a retail or logistics order. Whether it is a prescription order identifier is not established.

reasons: The label does not distinguish a prescription order from other orders.
Without a medical context no recorded context adds phi.
ambiguity.wouldSettle: A bounded definition of prescription-order signals and the medical context.

provenance.inference: The claim is unresolved in the record; no span asserted and only the pii domain is recorded. Authored by an AI agent run from the cited claims and case reasoning; no scanner output was consulted; unreviewed.

title: Member-shaped token under a group number label
rationale: Collision group member-id-vs-plan-identifier. FHIR distinguishes the insurer-assigned subscriber id from the coverage identifier. A group or policy label may name the coverage, not the person, so the member-id role is not established.

reasons: A group or policy number can identify a coverage shared by many people rather than one person.
Whether such an identifier is within the health plan beneficiary number category was not read.
ambiguity.wouldSettle: A source mapping coverage and group identifiers to the regulatory category.

provenance.inference: The distinction between Coverage.identifier and subscriberId is observed; applying it to a group label is project inference. Authored by an AI agent run from the cited claims and case reasoning; no scanner output was consulted; unreviewed.

title: Eight-digit reference that satisfies the check
rationale: Collision group card-vs-generic-number. A short run passes the check-digit test and falls inside the eight to nineteen digit range, so only the missing issuer evidence and the reference label argue against a card.

reasons: The check digit and length are satisfied, so structure alone does not exclude a card number.
Whether an issuer prefix beginning with 1 is allocated was not read.
ambiguity.wouldSettle: The ISO/IEC 7812 allocation table for the leading digit and a decision on the weight of a reference label.

provenance.inference: Check digit verified by hand; the claim is partial. The not-established identity reflects the unread allocation, not a finding that the number is a card. Authored by an AI agent run from the cited claims and case reasoning; no scanner output was consulted; unreviewed.
